verdict_reason: All four estimators are faithful and each was checked against an exact answer. The Hessian-vector product is BIT-IDENTICAL to the installed PyHessian's hessian_vector_product on the same vector (max absolute difference 0.000e+00, and the per-probe v^T H v agrees bit-for-bit on all 64 probes of a second independent pass). BLME's power iteration returns 0.611256087495 against the exact torch.linalg.eigvalsh top eigenvalue 0.611256087495 (relative error 1.09e-15) -- more accurate than PyHessian's own eigenvalues() call at 2.00e-06. SAM with p=2 returns 0.504999999999999 against the closed form 0.505 for L=||theta||^2/2 at theta=(3,4), rho=0.1 (9.99e-16), restoring theta to exactly [3.0, 4.0]. The Hutchinson estimator is unbiased (all four bias checks under 0.7 sigma over 40 seeds on two exactly-solvable anchors), and the dominant eigenvalue is returned SIGNED, not as a magnitude: on a negative-dominant anchor it gives -0.976781487465 against exact -0.976781583004 in 40/40 seeds.
comparable_reason: At the SHIPPED study config the headline eigenvalue's SIGN is set by the config, not by the model. On pythia-70m in bfloat16, top_eigenvalue_estimate is -104737 / -31942 / -105822 at n_power_iter=10 (study) and +111530 / +122867 / +110405 at n_power_iter=64 (repository default) for the same three seeds; the per-iteration Rayleigh quotient sweeps monotonically from -49751 at i=1 through a zero crossing near i=37 to +111530 at i=64, because the spectrum has a near-degenerate +/- pair at |lambda| ~ 1.24e5 that power iteration never separates. _meta_power_iter_converged is FALSE on 5 of 5 real models, so nothing in the output distinguishes a resolved model from an unresolved one. Separately, the curvature scale itself splits by architecture family: hutchinson_trace_estimate 135.6 / 194.1 / 17273.3 / 76497.1 for gpt2 / distilgpt2 / pythia-70m / pythia-160m, and _meta_hutchinson_trace_rel_se is 8.18 on pythia-70m -- eight times the magnitude of the estimate, whose sign flips across seeds (+17273, -31363, +16156).
github_reason: The pyhessian package imports from site-packages and I ran it directly on a 53-parameter double-precision MLP with an exactly formable Hessian: pyhessian.utils.hessian_vector_product vs BLME's _hvp on the same Rademacher vector gives max absolute difference 0.000e+00; pyhessian.hessian(...).eigenvalues(maxIter=200, tol=1e-12) returns 0.611254864982 where BLME returns 0.611256087495 and the exact eigenvalue is 0.611256087495, so BLME is the more accurate of the two; pyhessian .trace(maxIter=400) gives 1.582543973 against the exact 1.560585458 (1.41%), matching BLME's unbiased-but-noisy behaviour. A second independent pass re-implemented hessian.py verbatim (group_product, normalization with its s+1e-6, grad_outputs HVP, running-mean trace, top_n/tol eigenvalues) and confirmed trace parity at 0.000000e+00 across four config/anchor cells, with the only eigenvalue gap (2.06e-03) traced to the study's 10 iterations plus a one-iteration lag in where the Rayleigh quotient is evaluated (BLME post-update, PyHessian pre-update); at the repository's 64 iterations the two agree to 3.7e-06. At extreme scales BLME is STRICTLY BETTER than the reference: PyHessian's top eigenvalue collapses to exactly 0.0 at 4 of 8 fp32 ladder rungs (its normalization adds a hard 1e-6 and its group_product squares before summing) where BLME's _safe_norm path stays correct to 1.5e-06. I did not run google-research/sam, which is training code; SAM was checked against its closed form instead.
paper_reason: No published empirical value was reproduced. Foret et al. (arXiv:2010.01412) Table 11 reports a one-step CIFAR-10 estimated sharpness of 0.17 +/- 0.03 -- a different experiment on a different model class, so comparing it to language-model numbers would not be a reproduction. The anchors I do reproduce (SAM 0.505 to 9.99e-16, the exact top eigenvalue to 1.09e-15, the exact trace, an exact negative-dominant eigenvalue) are closed forms and reference-code agreement, not published figures.
confounds_reason: Curvature with respect to a weight block is a parameterisation-scale quantity and the families separate by three orders of magnitude (trace 135.6 / 194.1 / 17273.3 / 76497.1 across gpt2 / distilgpt2 / pythia-70m / pythia-160m). hutchinson_trace_per_param carries NO information on the real zoo: the last_layer scope has n_params = 7,087,872 for gpt2, distilgpt2 AND pythia-160m, so dividing is a near-constant rescale and its Spearman correlations against d_model, n_layers, vocab_size and parameter count are numerically IDENTICAL to the raw trace's at both n=4 and n=5. On a controlled synthetic width sweep (identical architecture, only d varies, d = 4..256) the raw trace has a log-log slope of +1.7831 with d (1,285x across the sweep) and the per-parameter form -0.1693 (0.391x) -- so the division removes most of the width dependence but over-corrects rather than reaching zero, and top_eigenvalue_estimate has no width normalisation at all. In the 4-5 model panel every |rho| of 0.866-0.894 sits in the vocab_size column, which takes only two values (50257 vs 50304) and is therefore a GPT-2-vs-Pythia family indicator, not a vocabulary effect.
defects: CONFIG / SAMPLING, the largest practical problem and NOT a code fault: the study override (beyond_benchmarks/configs/tasks.yaml:267-268) sets n_hutchinson=8 and n_power_iter=10 against repository defaults of 24 and 64. Consequences measured on real bfloat16 checkpoints: _meta_power_iter_converged is False on 5/5 models; top_eigenvalue_estimate CHANGES SIGN on pythia-70m between the two settings in 3/3 seeds (-104737 at 10, +111530 at 64); _meta_hutchinson_trace_rel_se is 8.18 on pythia-70m and 0.978 on gpt2-medium, and pythia-70m's trace sign flips across seeds. Reaching a 5% relative SE would need about 214,000 Hutchinson probes on pythia-70m against the shipped 8. The estimators are right; the shipped sample sizes do not resolve them, and to the task's credit both diagnostics are emitted.

CODE / THE CONVERGENCE FLAG DOES NOT TRACK ACCURACY: _meta_power_iter_converged was True in 0 of 120 runs on an anchor where the repository-default answer was exact to 4.30e-07 (tol 1e-7 against a measured rel_change of 1.109e-07), and on the anchor where it did fire (67/120) the median error when 'converged' (9.78e-08) was WORSE than when not (2.42e-08). It certifies successive-Rayleigh-quotient stationarity only: for H=diag(2,1) started at v=(1e-30,1) it reports eigenvalue 1.0, rel_change 0.0 and converged=true at both 10 and 64 iterations against a true dominant 2.0 (50% low). Add a residual test or a random restart, and detect the near-degenerate +/- pair explicitly.

CODE / THE EMITTED UNCERTAINTY UNDERSTATES THE REAL ONE: _meta_hutchinson_trace_rel_se is the within-run standard error of the probe mean, and over 40 seeds on two exactly-solvable anchors it is 11-22% below the actual run-to-run spread (0.179 emitted vs 0.202 measured; 0.261 vs 0.335; 0.141 vs 0.163; 0.252 vs 0.298). Directionally the right diagnostic, systematically optimistic.

CODE / MODULE-MODE RESTORATION, measured in both directions: sharpness.py:401 calls model.eval(), which recurses into every child, but the finally at :525-529 only calls model.train() when the ROOT was training. Exactly 1 of 7 modules is left mutated after a SUCCESSFUL run whether the child started in train or in eval; requires_grad (6/6), dtypes (6/6), parameter VALUES (6/6) and both global RNG states are restored. Consequence measured through blme.core.evaluate on gpt2 with transformer.drop preset to train: geometry_perplexity's ppl_rare_over_freq moves 1.43413995 -> 1.39333438 (-2.85%) and ppl_rare -2.10%, bit-reproducibly. On a stock HF checkpoint all flags are uniform, so the effect is 0; on real gpt2 and pythia-160m in bfloat16, 0 of 148 parameters and 0 of 152-164 modules were left changed and the 2 fp32 rotary buffers survived.

CODE / ROLLBACK SCOPE: model.eval() (:401), the requires_grad mutation (:405-409) and the float32 promotion (:432-435) all run BEFORE the try at :436. Raising inside that window leaves 3/6 requires_grad flags and 6/7 training flags wrong, and mid-promotion leaves 2/6 parameters stuck in float32 -- and core.py:439 catches the exception and CONTINUES the run with the same model object. An OOM during promotion is the realistic trigger, since it doubles parameter memory. Failures raised INSIDE the try are clean (0 requires_grad, 0 dtypes, 0 values, only the pre-existing 1/7 mode).

CODE / FP64 PROMOTION ROUND TRIP IS LOSSY: _promoted is decided from next(model.parameters()).dtype alone (:426-427). With a bf16 first parameter and a float64 parameter elsewhere, every parameter is cast to float32 and restored per-parameter, so the float64 one comes back with 65/66 elements changed (max absolute 6.500001e-11, max relative 2.746182e-09). The mirror case (float64 first, bf16 rest) skips promotion and the forward raises. bf16 -> fp32 -> bf16 is exactly lossless, so no real checkpoint is affected.

CODE / CRITICAL-STEP SEARCH WINDOW: _critical_step_size starts at eta0 = max(1e-6, 8*eps*||p||/||g||) and doubles in ONE direction 30 times, so its reachable window is [eta0/2^30, eta0*2^30]. NaN occurs exactly when the true eta* falls outside it -- predicted correctly in 16/16 ladder cells -- giving NaN at 3/8 fp32 and 6/8 fp64 rungs, and at 3/7 rungs of a controlled width sweep on a real cross-entropy loss. It is finite on 5/5 real checkpoints. Search in both directions from a bracketed estimate.
